context: Zoomable treemap data visualization showing a synthetic file system hierarchy with 471 files across 8 top-level directories, supporting click-to-zoom interaction with breadcrumb navigation
first_impression: A dense but well-structured treemap with deliberately crafted HCL-based color depth hierarchy and clean typographic treatment that reads as intentionally designed rather than default-generated.
what_works: The HCL lightness-by-depth system (L:45 for top dirs, L:60 for subdirs, L:72-82 for leaves) is genuinely clever — it encodes hierarchy in color without requiring a separate visual channel. Label fitting logic that hides text when cells are too small shows real craft. The Paul Tol colorblind-safe palette is a deliberate, non-default choice that pays off in harmonious distinction across 8 categories.
what_doesnt: The legend swatches use raw palette hex values while the treemap renders HCL-adjusted colors — so the legend colors visually mismatch the top-level directory fills (legend shows bright #4477AA, treemap renders a darker L:45 HCL variant). At the root zoom level, showing all three hierarchy levels simultaneously creates significant visual density — many leaf cells are too small to read and create noise that competes with the structural clarity the color system is working hard to establish.
